summary: A command-line tool that finds broken links in Markdown files.

files.README.md:
# linkcheck

Find broken links in your Markdown files before your readers do.

## Install

    pip install linkcheck

## Use

    linkcheck docs/

It prints one line per broken link with the file, the line number and the HTTP status,
and exits with code 1 if any link is broken, so you can run it in CI.

## Limits

- Only http and https links are checked. Relative links between files are not checked yet.
- Sites that block bots can show up as broken. Skip them with `--ignore example.com`.

## Contributing

Run `pip install -e .[dev]` then `pytest`. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
files.linkcheck/cli.py:
import argparse
import sys

from linkcheck.check import check_file, find_markdown


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="linkcheck", description="Find broken links in Markdown files.")
    parser.add_argument("path", help="a Markdown file or a folder")
    parser.add_argument("--ignore", action="append", default=[], help="skip links to this host")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=10.0)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    files = find_markdown(args.path)
    if not files:
        print(f"No Markdown files found in {args.path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    broken = 0
    for f in files:
        for problem in check_file(f, ignore=args.ignore, timeout=args.timeout):
            print(f"{f}:{problem.line}: {problem.url} ({problem.reason})")
            broken += 1
    print(f"Checked {len(files)} file(s), {broken} broken link(s).")
    return 1 if broken else 0
files.tests/test_check.py:
import httpx
import respx

from linkcheck.check import check_file, find_markdown


@respx.mock
def test_broken_link_is_reported_with_its_line(tmp_path):
    respx.head("https://ok.example/").mock(return_value=httpx.Response(200))
    respx.head("https://gone.example/").mock(return_value=httpx.Response(404))
    f = tmp_path / "a.md"
    f.write_text("[fine](https://ok.example/)\n[dead](https://gone.example/)\n")
    problems = check_file(f, ignore=[], timeout=1)
    assert [(p.line, p.reason) for p in problems] == [(2, "HTTP 404")]


@respx.mock
def test_ignored_hosts_are_skipped(tmp_path):
    f = tmp_path / "a.md"
    f.write_text("[dead](https://gone.example/)\n")
    assert check_file(f, ignore=["gone.example"], timeout=1) == []


def test_only_markdown_files_are_found(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "a.md").write_text("x")
    (tmp_path / "b.txt").write_text("x")
    assert [p.name for p in find_markdown(str(tmp_path))] == ["a.md"]
files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python: ["3.10", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - run: pip install -e .[dev]
      - run: pytest -q

demo.text: I run `pip install linkcheck`, then `linkcheck docs/` in my project.
It prints `docs/setup.md:14: https://old.example.com/guide (HTTP 404)` and `Checked 9 file(s), 1 broken link(s).`
I fix the link and run it again. It prints `Checked 9 file(s), 0 broken link(s).` and exits with code 0.
